loop.top3_why: The mean of the full pool is a simple, robust combination that performs consistently across all three validation windows (all ≈0.667). Given the unstable ranking and high correlation among many models, a plain mean is less likely to overfit the limited weight‑estimation data than the weighted inverse‑error scheme. DBA also performs well but its per‑window performance is more variable, and the mean offers a safer, more generalizable baseline for this seasonal‑dominated series.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B, while achieving the highest per‑window scores, relies on inverse‑error weighting on a pruned pool and thus is more sensitive to the high variance in weight estimation from only three windows; it also shows a larger gap to the best overall score. Candidate C (DBA) has the best composite score but its performance is uneven across windows, indicating potential over‑fitting to one window. Therefore the plain mean (A) is preferred for its stability and robustness.
